html:
Sivuqaq is the Yupik name for St. Lawrence Island in the Bering Sea, and the people there are the St. Lawrence Island Yupik. The island lies about 60 km from the Chukotka coast of Siberia, and its people speak the same Central Siberian Yupik language as their relatives across the strait, the Ungazigmit of Chukotka. They live by hunting walrus, seals and bowhead whales.

People have lived there for a very long time: the Old Bering Sea and Punuk cultures, ancestors of the Thule culture, are known from sites on the island. In 1878 to 1880, after whalers had killed much of the walrus herd, a famine killed a large part of the population. Today most people live in the villages of Gambell and Savoonga, in Alaska and the United States. See also Yup'ik and Cup'ik.
